question: The diagram on the right shows an L-shape made from four small squares. Ria wants to add an extra small square in order to form a shape with a line of symmetry. In how many different ways can she do this? <image1>
solution: The diagram is constructed from four small squares, each of which has at least one side in common with another small square. So Ria must place the extra small square so that it has a side in common with one of the existing squares. Ria can form three new shapes with a line of symmetry, as shown. ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-129.jpg?height=148&width=452&top_left_y=997&top_left_x=1386)
subject: combinatorial geometry
